items.title: Jimmy Cobb — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I don’t remember being there, but there used to be a saxophone player named Big Nick

ctx.x: In New York it was all over the place. There was Minton’s Playhouse. There was the Paradise, which was at 110th Street, I think, and what? – 110th and what? Eighth? Somewhere down there. I don’t remember being there, but there used to be a saxophone player named Big Nick, who used to have . . .

items.title: 67619_Big Nick Nicholas oral history interview
items.q: he and Jimmy introduced me to Eubie Blake... I'll never forget Jimmy Jones

ctx.x: Oh yeah, my wife and I both gave Speedy blood...no, gave Jimmy blood, you know what I mean, when he was ill there. But I knew Speedy well. Shoot. You know, go to her house, go to their house and they come to our house and have dinner. One of them type of things. You know. And he and Jimmy introduced me to Eubie Blake. He and Eubie was so tight. I went over to...it was in Brooklyn, on Hancock Street, so Jimmy says, "Come on, we're goin' to Eubie's house." So we go to Eubie's house and they're talking all this…

So then Eubie took us back in the room and he says this is the recipe when I was workin' in those after-hours joints in Baltimore. Man I looked at this, looked like ice cream. So I say, "What you goin' to do here?" So he put one teaspoon down there and I put that in my mouth and I thought the top of my head was comin' off. Hahahaha. He laughed. But then he and Jimmy got together there man, oh, it was somthin'. And so I'll never forget Jimmy Jones, you know, and Ellis Larkin. Ellis Larkin and...he's so marvelous,…
Yeah, Jimmy Cobb has spoken well of him.
